source.title: FedVSSAM: Mitigating Flatness Incompatibility in Sharpness-Aware Federated Learning
source.authors: Bing-Nan Xiao; Yuan Gao; Bing-Cong Li; Wei Ni; Xin Wang; Tony Q. S. Quek

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices. Some figure text is garbled in extraction; figure-only curves cannot be numerically reconstructed.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates flatness and generalization-related claims using federated sharpness-aware training, controlled comparisons, and measurements of flatness incompatibility and gradient tracking. It uses a different method and setting from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study does not test memorization of arbitrary labels, width beyond interpolation, CNN-versus-fully-connected performance, adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers, batch-size effects, dropout, or memorized-example removal. It tests flatness-related measurements from V7 in federated settings. Table 1 and the text report test accuracy comparisons, but not train-test gaps or magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness as V7 defines it. Its empirical flatness incompatibility and gradient tracking measurements are related, distinct constructs and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization premise to design a federated training algorithm and evaluates its performance and mechanism. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap correlation or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that a shared variance-suppressed direction mitigates flatness incompatibility, establish convergence and gradient-tracking bounds, and report better convergence and final accuracy in most tested cases. These conclusions do not establish V7.
record.recipe_differences: Federated learning with non-IID device data and partial participation; introduces variance-suppressed directions in SAM-based local search and updates. The claim versions primarily concern centralized model generalization properties.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report sensitivity to mixing coefficients γl and γg, local training epochs K, perturbation radius ρ, device participation, and heterogeneity level. Figure 9 reports accuracy sensitivity, while the text describes the trade-offs.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C.5 describes decreasing error between FedVSSAM's adjusted direction and an empirical IID reference gradient under both CIFAR-10 Dirichlet partitions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FedVSSAM increasingly tracks an IID reference gradient during the tested federated training runs.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C.5 describes low inter-device dispersion of local directional flatness proxies under both partitions; no numerical comparison with a control is supplied in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FedVSSAM exhibits low dispersion across devices' local directional loss-change estimates in the tested setting.

record.problems: The mechanism measurements are figure-only, with no numerical values recoverable from the supplied text or reported uncertainty. They use one architecture and CIFAR-10 with two Dirichlet partitions, and do not measure train-test gaps or the V7 sharpness statistic. The study reports test accuracy and standard deviations in tables for its proposed federated method and baselines, but these results do not test the claim versions listed.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results were omitted. Table 1, Table 3, and the ablation and sensitivity plots compare federated algorithms or the proposed method's components and report test accuracy or convergence, not a claim-version outcome; they are not included as rows. Appendix C.5's figure-only tracking and flatness-proxy results are retained as R1–R4 under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width beyond interpolation and the resulting test-error trajectory.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local-connectivity effects.

Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under the specified tuning regimes. FedAdam appears as a federated algorithm baseline, without an isolated comparison of the optimizer recipes named by V4.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus train–test gaps among comparably fitted networks, including comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V7 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. The local–global flatness argument concerns different objectives across devices, rather than a failure of V7's specified correlation. The supplied text supports qualitative diagnostic trends; exact figure values remain unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
CNN versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons and tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.

It studies empirical inter-device flatness incompatibility and global-direction tracking in federated SAM, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or train-test gaps across networks with similar training loss.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: FedVSSAM
rows.operation_detail: Measured global-direction tracking error between the adjusted direction and IID reference gradient over training rounds.

conditions.value: metrics every 80 training rounds; fixed subset of 50 devices; IID reference from 10 batches of size 512

rows.value: figure only; text says it keeps decreasing as training progresses
rows.note: The result measures direction tracking, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure or train-test gap.
rows.check: A diagnostic of the proposed training algorithm, not a claim-version outcome. The text reports decreasing gradient-tracking error, but this cannot establish V7.

rows.value: figure only; text says it yields a low proxy as training progresses
